Now the both_leaves_open parameter is being used! The change adds a condition `and not both_leaves_open` to the if statement that handles double windows doors.

The logic is:
- The existing code partitions double windows doors into two leaves, removes the larger one, and uses the smaller one as a blocker
- This new condition means: only do that partitioning if both_leaves_open is False
- When both_leaves_open is True, the double windows door handling is skipped, so both vantails will be open and the passage will be bounded only by walls/windows

The comment explains this: "When both_leaves_open=True (e.g. terrace doors), both vantails open so the passage is bounded only by walls/windows."

This is implementing the feature - the actual logic change to support the new parameter.

<summary>
  <request>Implement both_leaves_open feature for terrace door width measurements to correctly measure double windows doors</request>
  <investigated>Examined terrace_doors.py, door_size.py, and _run_cache.py source code to understand door measurement algorithm. Analyzed orthogonal probe sliding technique, double windows door partitioning logic, and per-run memoization infrastructure. Ran initial tests discovering old single-leaf measurements of ~74.6cm. Reviewed test reference files to understand expected behaviors across multiple architectural plans.</investigated>
  <learned>Double windows door measurement previously treated smaller leaf as blocker, measuring only through larger opening (~74.6cm). PMR rule 33.16.62.10 requires measuring with both vantails open for accessibility. The orthogonal probe technique slides perpendicular to door axis until hitting walls/windows. When both_leaves_open=True, leaf partitioning is skipped and passage measures wall-to-wall. Measurements consistently double to ~149.5cm when both leaves open, converting failing doors to passing. Door_size uses cached_per_run decorator for performance optimization during recursive analysis calls.</learned>
  <completed>Implemented both_leaves_open parameter in analyze_door_size function with logic to skip double-door leaf partitioning when True. Updated terrace_doors.py to call analyze_door_size with both_leaves_open=True. Updated test references for 3 plans: DCE-Batiment_AB (1 door: 74.6→149.5cm), 04_PLAN_R1 (1 door: 94.0→94.3cm), and 18-130-DCE-Batiment_AB_half1 (4 doors: all 74.6→~149.5cm). All previously failing double doors now pass 80cm threshold. Generated updated visual artifacts showing new measurements.</completed>
  <next_steps>Awaiting test suite completion running in background to verify all terrace_doors tests pass with updated references. May inspect visual SVG outputs to confirm measurements render correctly. Work on fix_pmr_v2_again branch with 1 commit ahead of origin.</next_steps>
  <notes>The both_leaves_open feature represents a significant regulatory interpretation correction—measuring terrace doors with both vantails open rather than single-leaf provides the true accessible passage width. Width measurements doubled consistently (~2x) across all affected double doors. One test (2-6_EXE-DET_OPAC73) already passed, likely having single doors or already-compliant widths. The 04_PLAN_R1 door showed only minor variation (0.3cm), suggesting it may not be a double door affected by the new logic.</notes>
</summary>
